help.title: How to command
help.talk.body: You are Hammer. You never act on a unit directly: you call a station on the radio and it decides how to carry out the order. Type a call in the box and send it (Enter, or the Send button), or hold the microphone button (on a keyboard, the ` key), speak, and release: the call is sent as soon as it is transcribed. Picking a squad on the map, then a point, then Hold, Move or Attack writes the call and sends it for you; with a squad picked, a spoken order that names nobody goes to it. On a keyboard, Up and Down in the box bring back earlier calls. Call Anvil, your operator, for anything that is not one squad's job.
help.attack.say: Viper 1, this is Hammer. Attack Foxtrot. Over.
help.upgrade: Give a squad a smarter brain
help.all.say: All stations, this is Hammer. Attack Zulu. Over.
help.strict.1: A callsign and the order are enough, and a callsign that is only spelled or heard roughly right is corrected. With no callsign, Anvil gets the message.
help.strict.2: Every call opens with who you are calling and who you are: "Viper 1, this is Hammer."
help.strict.3: Full procedure: the opening call, and Over or Out at the end. Anything else is refused.
help.more.body: Black ground has never been seen, dim ground was seen earlier, and clear ground is in sight of your troops right now. Land rigs are captured by infantry and sea rigs by boats; each one pumps gold. You win by destroying the enemy headquarters or by holding more points when the clock runs out.

tut.title: Lesson
tut.learnAbout: A first match with a coach: you give real orders to real squads, against an enemy that waits for you.
tut.againAbout: Five minutes with a coach, in a match of its own.
tut.welcome: You are {me}, the commander. You never move troops yourself: you give orders on the radio, and each squad's leader carries them out.
tut.select: Start a call: click one of your squads, on the map or in the {squads} list.
tutTouch.select: Start a call: tap one of your squads on the map.
tut.order: Now click {first} on the map and choose {hold}: the call is sent at once. You can also just type it: “{squad} hold {firstName}”.
tutTouch.order: Now tap {first} on the map and choose {hold}: the call is sent at once.
tut.answer: {squad} answers “Wilco”: it will do it. Squads answer you on the radio, and call again when they arrive, meet the enemy or take losses.
tut.orders: Three orders: Hold takes a point and defends it, Move goes there without fighting, Attack goes in fighting. Orders go to the named points (A · Alpha to Z · Zulu) or at an enemy you can see, never to open ground.
tut.capture: Gold comes from oil rigs. Send {other} to hold {rig}: a squad that stands on it alone for {seconds} seconds captures it.
tut.fog: {rig} is yours: +{income} gold a second. Black map was never seen, dim map was seen earlier, bright map is in sight now. Your squads and the points you hold are your eyes.
tut.buy: New squads are bought by {anvil}, your operator. Click {unit} under {build}: the button writes the radio call for you.
tutTouch.buy: New squads are bought by {anvil}, your operator. Open {buildTab} and tap {unit}: the button writes the radio call for you.
tut.deploy: {anvil} bought it and the squad is deploying: watch the bar fill. {anvil} buys only when you order it, unless you hand it the whole fight (“{anvil}, run the fight”).
tut.upgrade: Each squad's leader is an AI. An upgrade gives it a stronger one: tier 2 for {cost2} gold, tier 3 for {cost3}. Click ▲ beside a squad in the {squads} list. The list shows the new tier.
tutTouch.upgrade: Each squad's leader is an AI. An upgrade gives it a stronger one: tier 2 for {cost2} gold, tier 3 for {cost3}. Open {squads} and tap ▲ beside a squad. The list shows the new tier.
tut.enemy: An enemy squad is coming for {rig}. Once you can see it, it has a name on the map, like “{target}”. Pick a squad, click the enemy, and choose {attack}.
tutTouch.enemy: An enemy squad is coming for {rig}. Once you can see it, it has a name on the map, like “{target}”. Tap a squad, tap the enemy, then {attack}.
tut.voice: You can also talk: hold the microphone (on a keyboard, the ` key), say the order, and let go. “{procedure}” sets how formal a call must be; relaxed needs only a callsign and the order.
tut.win: You win by destroying the enemy headquarters, or by holding more points when the clock runs out. That is the whole game; Help has more example calls.
help.q.move: Can I send troops anywhere, or only to the points?
help.a.move: Only to the named points on the map (A · Alpha to Z · Zulu) and at enemy squads you can see, which get names like “Target 3”. There is no order to open ground: the squad's leader chooses the route and where to stand.
help.q.auto: Why do squads sometimes appear that I did not buy?
help.a.auto: Anvil buys only on your order. The one exception is when you hand it the fight (“Anvil, run the fight”): then it buys and sends squads as it sees fit, until you take the fight back.
help.q.upgrade: How do I know an upgrade is happening?
help.a.upgrade: Press ▲ on a squad and send the call. The button shows the request while Anvil decides; when the gold is spent, the squad's tier changes in the list and the log says so. An upgrade gives that squad's leader a stronger AI model: tier 2 plans further ahead, tier 3 further still.
help.q.speed: Can a match run slower or faster?
help.a.speed: Yes. The speed is chosen on the start screen when you make a match, together with its length and how hard the scripted enemy presses.
help.a.units: Five units a side. Aegis: commandos, main battle tank, patrol boat, attack helicopter and precision rocket launcher. Ashfall: militia, technical, speedboat, drone swarm and rocket team. Aircraft cross land and sea; the rocket launcher outranges everything but needs another squad to spot for it; the rocket team is for armour.

lobby.speedAbout.relaxed: The clock runs slower. Squad leaders still take a few real seconds to think, so they answer sooner in game terms: the easiest pace to command at.
lobby.speedAbout.normal: The pace the game is balanced for.
lobby.speedAbout.fast: The clock runs half as fast again. Squad leaders still take a few real seconds to think, so they answer later in game terms, and more rides on the orders you gave beforehand.
